metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: does a repeatable, domain-specific Claude capability like client-review mean Claude is analyzing the portfolio and deciding what matters for the meeting, or is it just a plain-text file of instructions Claude reads and follows? beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude's client-review capability was a built-in portfolio analysis app — a black box that thinks about the account. It isn't. It's a plain-text file Claude reads before it works. So here's the real question: does that file put a portfolio analyst inside Claude, or does it just assemble the meeting?

beats.narration_text: Here's the actual object. A skill is a folder. This one is called client-review. The SKILL.md file inside holds the whole instruction set — plain English, no hidden logic, no secret model of the portfolio. Claude reads that file, then acts. The file is the program.

The pipeline lives in the file's Steps section. Claude reads it, runs each step in the order written, returns the result. No branching, no side thought — unless a step itself says branch. They optimized for repeatability over cleverness, and this is what that choice looks like.

Client-review's SKILL.md names exactly what the packet contains: a portfolio performance summary, allocation analysis, talking points, action items — ready before quarterly reviews, annual checkups, or an ad-hoc client meeting. Feed it the same account data twice, and it builds the same meeting-ready packet twice; that's what the coverage bought you. Ask for something the file never mentions — a comparison it doesn't list, a chart it doesn't call for — and there's nothing to fall back on. Claude reasons past the file on its own, and that's where the repeatability stops.

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill isn't a hidden analysis app. It's a plain-text file of instructions, and that's what buys you the repeatability: same account data, same meeting-ready packet, every run. Whatever the file doesn't say, Claude works out on its own — and that part won't repeat.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: write a SKILL.md for a recurring meeting I prep for. List exactly what must appear every time, then list what would be left to my judgment because the file doesn't cover it. Read the two lists back — the first is what repeats identically every run; the second is where Claude is reasoning past the file, not following it. Go deeper: take one item off the judgment list, write it into the file as a new step, and see whether the packet still feels like yours or starts feeling like the file's.
